summary: Embedding header/annotation bleed into vector payload causing reranker score skew
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring quality regression in reranker results for long-document search queries. Investigation shows certain embedding vectors include non-numeric header annotations embedded into the binary payload at batch boundaries, which downstream post-processing did not strip.

Impact:
- Customer search relevance dropped by ~12% on A/B test; intermittent but reproducible for batches containing mixed legacy and new ingestion pipelines.
- Users observing unexpected top-k order flips and occasional NaN scores in reranker logs.
- Affects live prod traffic for Chronicle Health (enterprise contract).

Environment:
- Production, us-west cluster, serving-runtime revision r2026.2.1, api-gateway v1.14.
- Embeddings produced by text-embed-legacy-v1 via an internal migration job that mixes older clients and new SDKs.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run embed ingestion job that batches 1k docs where first half were produced by legacy agent (SDK v0.9) and second half by new SDK (v1.3).
2) Send batch through /v1/embeddings endpoint with header annotations enabled (X-Embed-Meta).
3) Fetch reranker results for a stable set of queries and compare top-10 ordering.
4) Observe rerank ordering flips and occasionally NaN/Inf scores in logs.

Observed logs/snippets:
- reranker: score_computation: encountered non-numeric token at index 0 of vector payload (converted to 0.0)
- ingest: "WARN embedding: stray-header 'X-Embed-Tag' bytes detected at offset 128"
- api-gateway: logs show mixed Content-Length/Trailer usage on affected requests.

Notes:
- Customer provided a sample payload and query set (attached to ticket).
- Problem appears to correlate with batches created by the migration job that retains annotation headers on a per-document basis but when packed into the binary vector buffer the header bytes are not isolated and leak into the vector bytes.

investigation_notes: Binary inspection of sample batch shows ASCII header fragments ('X-Embed-Tag:') embedded at vector offsets for certain docs.

The serializer used a fixed padding scheme; legacy SDK emitted headers into padding rather than separate metadata field when header flag set. New serializer assumed padding is zeroed and did not sanitize before concatenation.
Reproducible when batch ordering mixes legacy and new SDK payloads and when packing alignment crosses a 128-byte boundary due to Content-Length vs. chunked transfer differences.
Hypothesis: api-gateway Trailer handling change introduced a different chunking behavior leading to padding bytes being preserved instead of zeroed out.
resolution_notes: Hotfix deployed to serving-runtime r2026.2.2 that sanitizes padding regions and explicitly strips known header annotations before vector concatenation.
API gateway config reverted to ensure consistent chunk framing for a 2-hour maintenance window while we roll the hotfix (non-disruptive to tenant routing).

Customer-side mitigation: Provided a short-term SDK patch (v0.9.3) that ensures legacy agent zeroes padding and exposes a compatibility flag; Chronicle Health validated canary and metrics returned to baseline.
Follow-ups: Add ingestion regression test that simulates mixed-SDK batches and chunked transfer edge cases; owner: Lena Park; due: 2026-03-20.
Postmortem planned and linked to CON-embed-ingest-2026-03 (confluence page).
